info.title: Deutero Study Management API
info.description:
API for the full study lifecycle on the Deutero research platform:

1. **Projects & Studies** — create and configure studies.
2. **Welcome & Consent** — the message (and consent gate) participants see first.
3. **Screening** — qualifying questions that gate participation.
4. **Characteristics** — participant attribute questions (segmentation).
5. **Interview Questions** — the linear main question list the AI interviewer follows.
5b. **Interview Flow** — the branching alternative to the linear list: steps,
   conditional paths, captured answers, data fetches, and webhooks.
6. **Recruitment** — participation links, short URLs, and response quotas.
7. **Embed** — publishable keys and install snippets for embedding the widget.
8. **Response Monitoring** — stats, interviews, and transcripts.
8b. **Personas & Simulation** — AI participants and simulated interview runs for
    rehearsing a study before recruiting.
9. **Transcript Search** — bulk transcript export plus string, semantic
   (embedding), and hybrid search over participant answers.
10. **Analysis & Clustering** — per-question aggregations (scale/options
    tallies) and k-means clustering over response embeddings.
11. **Webhooks** — organization-level event subscriptions, so your systems hear
    about a finished interview (or a filled study) without polling.

## Authentication

Provide an API key (from the dashboard settings page) in the `X-API-Key`
header, or as a `Bearer` token. Stytch M2M access tokens are also accepted as
Bearer tokens.
info.x-cli-description: Every Deutero endpoint, plus the flow-behavior and fielding answers that only exist once your research corpus is sitting in a local database.

get.description: List every project in the caller's organization.

post.description: Create a new project owned by the caller's organization.

patch.description: Update a project's name and/or description. Omitted fields are untouched.

post.description:
Create a new study inside a project. The study starts with an empty main
question list; configure the rest of the lifecycle with the Welcome,
Screening, Characteristics, Questions, Recruitment, and Embed endpoints.

Interview mode is **linear** (ordered question list).

get.description: Full study configuration, including per-lifecycle-stage status (welcome configured, screening/characteristics enabled and question counts, main question count) and participation links.

patch.description: Partial update of study properties. Only fields present in the request body are changed. A ``redirect_url`` is normalized on the way in: a single-braced ``{external_participant_id}`` is corrected to the ``{{external_participant_id}}`` the interviewer substitutes, and anything else in double braces is kept but named in ``redirect_url_warning``.

put.description:
Create or replace the study's welcome/consent message. Set ``consent`` to true
to require participants to explicitly agree before the interview begins.
put.x-pp-example: deutero-pp-cli studies welcome set f0ed9214-06fc-4420-87b3-31240b670fc1 --message example

put.description: Upserts the translation for ``target_language`` (one translation per target language). The welcome message must be set first.
put.x-pp-example: deutero-pp-cli studies welcome upsert-translation f0ed9214-06fc-4420-87b3-31240b670fc1 --target-language example --translation-text example

get.description: Settings plus the ordered screening question list.

put.description: Enable/disable screening and set the disqualification message and redirect URL. Disabling preserves questions and settings. The redirect URL may carry ``{{external_participant_id}}``, replaced at screen-out time with the id this interview arrived with, so a panel callback can say who bounced as well as who finished. It is the only placeholder understood: a single-braced ``{external_participant_id}`` is corrected to it, and any other ``{{…}}`` is stored untouched but named in ``redirect_url_warning``.
put.x-pp-example: deutero-pp-cli studies screening set-settings f0ed9214-06fc-4420-87b3-31240b670fc1 --enabled True

get.description: The study's main questions, resolved and in interview order.

post.description:
Create a question and append it to the end of the study's question list.

Set ``qtype`` and provide only the config fields that type needs. If ``qtype``
is omitted the type is inferred from which fields you send: ``scale`` → scale,
``options`` → choices, ``slots`` → slots, ``expected_image`` → image_upload,
otherwise text.

Example bodies:

* **Open text** — `{"question": "Walk me through your last purchase.", "follow_up": true, "max_turns": 6}`
* **Scale** — `{"question": "How satisfied are you?", "qtype": "scale", "scale": {"minScale": 1, "maxScale": 5, "minLabel": "Not at all", "maxLabel": "Very"}}`
* **Single choice** — `{"question": "Which plan are you on?", "qtype": "choices", "options": ["Basic", "Pro"]}`
* **Multi-select** — `{"question": "Which features do you use?", "qtype": "multi_select", "options": ["Search", "Export", "API"], "min_select": 1, "max_select": 2}`
* **Card sort** — `{"question": "Sort these into buckets.", "qtype": "card_sort", "options": ["Apple", "Carrot"], "groups": ["Fruit", "Vegetable"]}`

example.question: How did you first hear about us?

post.x-pp-example: deutero-pp-cli studies questions create f0ed9214-06fc-4420-87b3-31240b670fc1 --question "How did you first hear about us?"

patch.description: Partial update. Pass an empty list to clear ``options``/``slots``/``groups``.

delete.description: Removes the question, its attached images, and its list entry; remaining questions are renumbered.

put.description: Supply every question ID in the desired interview order.

post.description:
Review the study's questions before it goes live, the same check the dashboard's
**Validate** button runs.

Returns three things:

* **Ethics** — one pass/fail for the whole set, with the specific concerns when it
  fails (offensive or intrusive wording, targeting under-13s, asking for
  identifying, financial, or medical details, requesting explicit images).
* **Language quality** — per question, any clarity, grammar, or spelling problem,
  judged in the study's own language.
* **Redundancy** — per question, which other questions it overlaps with and how.

Findings carry both the question's ``number`` (1-based interview order) and its
``question_id``, so you can act on them with ``PATCH .../questions/{question_id}``.
Nothing is changed by this call, and no result is stored — it is advisory only.

This is a model call over the whole question set, so it typically takes ten to
twenty seconds.

get.description:
The study's interview flow, in the same shape `set_graph` accepts — so you can
read it, change part of it, and write it back.

Also reports whether the flow is the study's active interview script
(`interview_mode`), and its `graph_version`, which you can pass to `set_graph`
or `patch_graph` to avoid overwriting an edit made in the browser meanwhile.

`flow` is null when the study has no interview flow yet; it still runs its
linear question list, and `import_questions_to_graph` will turn that list into
a starting flow.

put.description:
Write a complete interview flow, replacing whatever is stored.

**Nothing is saved unless the flow is valid** — on any problem this returns 422
with the same error list `check_graph` gives, and the stored flow is untouched.

Steps are connected two different ways, and mixing them up is the most common
mistake:

* `start`, `end`, `question` and `decision` steps sit on the interview's path
  and are connected with `edges`.
* `extract` and `webhook` steps attach to a question with `"after": "<question
  id>"`, and `context_fetch` attaches with `"before": "<question id>"`. They are
  never listed in `edges`; the compiler splices them into the right place.

A minimal branching flow:

```json
{"flow": {"nodes": [
  {"id": "start", "type": "start"},
  {"id": "q_pets", "type": "question",
   "config": {"qtype": "options", "text": "Do you have pets?",
              "options": ["Yes", "No"], "output_var": "has_pets"}},
  {"id": "branch", "type": "decision", "config": {"mode": "deterministic"}},
  {"id": "q_story", "type": "question",
   "config": {"qtype": "open_ended", "text": "Tell me about your pet."}},
  {"id": "q_ideal", "type": "question",
   "config": {"qtype": "open_ended", "text": "Describe your ideal pet."}},
  {"id": "end", "type": "end"}
], "edges": [
  {"from": "start", "to": "q_pets"},
  {"from": "q_pets", "to": "branch"},
  {"from": "branch", "to": "q_story",
   "condition": {"var": "has_pets", "op": "eq", "value": "Yes"}, "priority": 0},
  {"from": "branch", "to": "q_ideal", "default": true, "priority": 1},
  {"from": "q_story", "to": "end"},
  {"from": "q_ideal", "to": "end"}
]}}
```

Use `{{captured_answer}}` in question text to pipe an earlier answer in. The
validator enforces that a captured answer is only used where it is guaranteed
to exist.

Saving does not switch the study into graph mode — call `activate_graph` for
that. The flow is fully editable afterwards in the browser flow editor, and
step ids, positions and webhook signing secrets survive round trips.

patch.summary: Edit parts of a study's interview flow
patch.description:
Apply targeted edits to the stored flow instead of rewriting it — safer than
read-modify-write on a large flow, and it leaves untouched steps exactly as the
researcher arranged them.

Operations are applied in order to the stored flow, then the **result is
validated as a whole**, so passing through an invalid intermediate state is
fine. As with `set_graph`, nothing is saved unless the end state is valid.

* `{"op": "add_node", "node": {...}}`
* `{"op": "update_node", "id": "q_pets", "config": {"text": "New wording?"}}` —
  merges into the step's config; omitted keys keep their value, `null` clears one
* `{"op": "remove_node", "id": "q_pets"}` — also drops its connections and
  detaches anything attached to it
* `{"op": "add_edge", "edge": {"from": "branch", "to": "q_ideal", "default": true}}`
* `{"op": "update_edge", "from": "branch", "to": "q_story", "condition": {...}}`
* `{"op": "remove_edge", "from": "branch", "to": "q_story"}`

Example — rewording a question and raising its turn limit:

```json
{"ops": [{"op": "update_node", "id": "q_story",
          "config": {"text": "Tell me more about your pet.", "max_turns": 6}}]}
```

get.summary: Get a flow's signal (webhook) delivery settings
get.description:
The delivery config behind every "Send a signal" (`webhook`) step in the saved
flow, **including the signing secret** each step's deliveries are signed with.

A signal is fired by the interviewer mid-interview, at the point in the flow
where the step sits — distinct from the organization-level webhooks (the
Webhooks endpoints), which this dashboard fires for lifecycle events like
`interview.completed`. The secret is minted the first time the step is saved
and kept stable across later saves, so a receiver configured once keeps
verifying.

Verify each delivery's `webhook-signature` against the secret for the step that
sent it before acting on the body, and dedupe on `webhook-id`. To see what a
particular interview actually sent, and whether it was accepted, use
`get_interview_fetches_and_signals`.

post.summary: Check an interview flow without saving it
post.description:
Validate a flow and report every problem, changing nothing. Use this while
drafting: iterate here until `valid` is true, then save with `set_graph`.

Pass the flow in `flow`, or omit it to re-check the study's stored flow.

Each problem names the step it is on using **your own step ids**, a stable
`code`, and a plain-language `message`. Common codes:

* `no_default` — a decision step has several paths but no `"default": true` one
* `unreachable` / `no_path_to_end` — a step can't be reached, or can't reach an end
* `var_not_guaranteed` — a step uses a captured answer that earlier branching
  means might not exist yet
* `unattached` — an extract/webhook/context_fetch step is missing `after`/`before`
* `missing_max_revisits` — a step inside a loop has no repeat limit
* `private_url` — a fetch or webhook URL points at an internal address

When the flow is valid, `compiled` shows the derived captured-answer table and
the final execution order with side steps spliced into place — worth checking
that attachments landed where you intended.

post.summary: Seed an interview flow from the study's question list
post.description:
Build a straight-line flow from the study's existing linear questions —
start → each question in order → end — and save it, **replacing any flow the
study already has**.

The usual starting point: you get a flow that behaves exactly like the current
interview, then add branching to it with `patch_graph`. Each question captures
its answer as `q1`, `q2`, … so you can branch on them or pipe them into later
question text straight away.

Does not change the study's interview mode; call `activate_graph` when ready.

post.summary: Run interviews from the interview flow
post.description:
Switch the study to `graph` mode: interviews follow the stored flow instead of
the linear question list. Requires a flow that last saved without problems.

The question list is left untouched — `deactivate_graph` switches back to it at
any time.

post.summary: Run interviews from the linear question list
post.description: Switch the study back to `linear` mode. The stored flow is kept, just not used.

get.summary: Describe every interview flow step type
get.description:
The configuration schema for every step type an interview flow can contain,
generated from the same registry the validator enforces — so it cannot drift
from what `check_graph` will accept.

Read this before authoring a flow. It returns, per step type: what the step
does, whether it sits on the interview path or attaches to a question (and with
`after` or `before`), and every config field with its type, whether it is
required, and what it means. Plus the valid question types, condition
operators, decision modes, merge modes, the built-in variables available to
piped text, and the structural rules the validator applies.

schema.title: Response Describe Graph Nodes Api V1 Graph Node Types Get

get.description: Participation links, quota status, and pre-interview gate flags. The links come back bare: append ``&source=<your campaign tag>`` and/or ``&participant_id=<your id for this person>`` to attribute the arrival — they are recorded on the interview as ``web_source`` and ``external_participant_id``, and can be read back and filtered on. ``participant_id`` here is your own free-text id, not the Deutero participant UUID of the same name.

put.description:
Set a custom short-link slug, the response quota, and/or the post-completion
redirect URL. Omitted fields are untouched; set ``clear_max_responses`` to
true to remove the quota. The slug must be unique across all studies.

The redirect URL may carry ``{{external_participant_id}}``, which is replaced
at the end of the interview with the id that interview arrived with (from the
link's ``?participant_id=`` or the embed metadata bag) — the usual way to hand
a panel or CRM its own id back on completion. It expands to the empty string
for an interview that carried no id, so a callback that requires one should be
built from links that always set it.

``{{external_participant_id}}`` is the only placeholder either redirect
understands. A single-braced ``{external_participant_id}`` is corrected to it
(a URL stored with the literal text would silently never substitute); any
other ``{{…}}`` is stored untouched but named in ``redirect_url_warning``,
which is null when the URL was stored exactly as sent.

get.description: Every embed key owned by the caller's organization (secrets omitted).

post.description:
Create a publishable embed key for the caller's organization, optionally
pinned to one study.

**The response includes ``publishable_key`` and ``signing_secret`` — this is
the only time they are returned. Store them immediately.**

schema.title: Response Create Embed Key Api V1 Embed Keys Post

patch.description: Change allowed origins, revoke/reactivate (``status``), or adjust the metadata size limit.

schema.title: Response Update Embed Key Api V1 Embed Keys  Key Id  Patch

get.description:
Generate the HTML install snippet for embedding this study's interview widget.

Pass ``publishable_key`` (from key creation) to fill it into the snippet;
otherwise a placeholder is emitted. ``mode`` selects the widget presentation
(default ``chat``). The signed-token variant is also returned for servers that
mint per-visitor JWS (HS256) tokens with the key's signing secret.

**Metadata.** Both snippets can carry context that is stored with the interview
and shown alongside the transcript (plan, tenant, seat count, and so on). The
basic snippet includes a ``data-metadata`` placeholder holding an example flat
JSON object — replace its keys with your own, or delete the attribute if you
have no context to attach.

* ``data-metadata`` is **page-supplied and therefore untrusted**: a visitor can
  change it with browser dev tools before the interview starts. That is fine for
  context you only want to read next to the transcript. It is not fine when the
  interview has to act on the value — asking enterprise-only questions, skipping
  a section for trial users, or reporting results split by plan.
* For those cases use ``signed_snippet`` instead of the basic one: your server
  mints a short-lived token (HS256, ``kid`` header = the publishable key,
  ``sub`` = your stable end-user id, ``exp`` no more than 900s after ``iat``)
  with a ``metadata`` claim, signed with that key's signing secret, and the page
  sends it as ``data-signed-token`` in place of ``data-publishable-key``. Those
  values are recorded with provenance ``"token"`` (shown as verified in the
  dashboard) and override any page-supplied value of the same name, so a tag may
  carry ``data-metadata`` as well when some values need not be verified.
* ``participant_id`` is the one key with a meaning of its own: whatever value
  it holds is also stored on the interview as ``external_participant_id``, so
  an embedded study can be joined back to your own users the same way a link
  built with ``?participant_id=`` can. It stays in the metadata bag as well.
  Page-supplied it is no more trustworthy than any other key — it labels the
  row and identifies nobody; send it in the signed token when it has to be
  verified. Keep it pseudonymous either way (a hash of your user id, not an
  email): it is stored on the interview, exported, and sent on the
  ``interview.completed`` webhook.
* Limits, enforced at bootstrap — a payload that breaks any of them is rejected
  outright, so validate before you send: at most 32 keys; key names match
  ``^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$``; scalar values only (string <= 1 KB, number,
  bool, null) — no nested objects or arrays; total serialized size <= the key's
  ``metadata_max_bytes``.

get.description: Every persona defined for the study, newest first.

post.description:
Write a persona by hand. Describe the participant the way you would brief an actor — who they are, what they are dealing with, how they feel about the subject — since that description is the only thing shaping their answers.

Example: `{"content": "A 34-year-old ICU nurse in Leeds, six years on the job, sceptical of new scheduling software after a botched rollout last year. Blunt, short on time, warms up when asked about patient safety."}`

example.content: How did you first hear about us?

post.x-pp-example: deutero-pp-cli studies personas create f0ed9214-06fc-4420-87b3-31240b670fc1 --content "How did you first hear about us?"

patch.description: Replace a persona's description. Simulations already run keep the text they ran against — this only affects future runs.

example.content: How did you first hear about us?

patch.x-pp-example: deutero-pp-cli studies personas update f0ed9214-06fc-4420-87b3-31240b670fc1 5f8e4e84-aa61-42f5-81ed-67cd6afdd87a --content "How did you first hear about us?"

delete.description: Interviews already simulated with this persona are kept.

post.description:
Draft personas from the study's own context — its type, description, research question, objectives and target population — so they resemble the people you intend to recruit. Fill those fields in on the study first; a sparse study yields generic personas.

Generated personas are saved to the study by default (``source: 'generated'``); pass ``save: false`` to preview them without storing anything.

Start one simulated interview and return immediately — the run continues in the background, so poll ``GET /simulations/{simulation_id}`` for its outcome.

Credits are reserved at the estimated cost before the run starts; a request that would exceed the balance is refused with 402 and costs nothing. Plan limits apply: simulations are not available on Hobby, and the standard/premium tiers need Solo/Team.

Run one persona per call; to sweep a panel, call once per persona.

get.description: Every simulation run for the study, newest first, with the interview each produced and what it cost.

One run's current state. Poll this after starting a run: ``running`` until the interview finishes, then ``completed`` (with ``credits_used``) or ``failed`` (reservation released, nothing charged — ``error`` says why).

delete.description: Removes the run's bookkeeping row. The interview it produced is kept — delete that separately if you want the transcript gone. A run still in flight cannot be deleted.

get.description: Counts of started/completed/incomplete interviews, completion rate, and quota fill relative to ``max_responses``. Simulated (persona) interviews are counted separately.

Interviews for a study, newest first. Filter by completion status, simulation flag, and start-time range. Each row carries where the participant arrived from — ``web_source`` (the entry link's ?source= tag), ``external_participant_id`` (its ?participant_id=, or the embed metadata bag's participant_id key) and ``referrer``. Pass ``external_participant_id`` to look up one person's interviews by your own id for them.

get.summary: Look up interviews by your own participant id
get.description:
Every interview in this study that arrived carrying ``external_participant_id`` — your own id for the person, from the entry link's ``?participant_id=`` or the embed metadata bag's ``participant_id`` key — in full detail, newest first. The direct answer to "did this person finish, and what happened?" when you hold your id for them and not ours.

Expect more than one row sometimes: a person who abandons and starts again has an interview per attempt, and ``total`` says how many. An empty list means nobody has arrived on a link carrying that id — not that they were screened out. For the transcripts behind these interviews, pass the same id to ``bulk_transcripts``; for one interview's messages, ``get_transcript`` with the id from a row here.

The match is exact, and the id is participant-supplied text: it says which of your own records to look at, it does not authenticate anybody.

parameters.name: external_participant_id

schema.description: Your own id for the participant, exactly as the entry link or embed metadata carried it
schema.title: External Participant Id

parameters.description: Your own id for the participant, exactly as the entry link or embed metadata carried it

get.description: One interview with its screening answers, participant characteristics, embed-widget metadata (with per-key provenance), message count, and the answers it captured into Interview Flow variables. ``web_source``, ``external_participant_id`` and ``referrer`` say where the participant arrived from: the first two are set by building the entry link with ``?source=`` and ``?participant_id=`` (or, for an embedded study, a ``participant_id`` key in the widget's metadata bag). All three are participant-supplied text — labels to join on, never proof of who answered.

All messages in chronological order. ``type`` distinguishes interviewer questions from participant answers; internal tool/thinking payloads are not included, including the canonical form of a structured answer (the participant's own words are kept). ``variables`` carries the answers the interview captured into Interview Flow variables — the structured values behind the conversation, empty for a study that captures nothing. ``decisions`` says how each Branch was decided: the label the classifier emitted, whether it matched a path or fell through to the 'otherwise' one, and the step chosen. Graph step ids are the ones you authored, so they can be passed back to search or clustering.

get.summary: Get an interview's data fetches and signals
get.description: What an Interview Flow's side steps did outside the conversation: every 'Bring in data' (context_fetch) request with the response it returned or the error it hit, and every 'Send a signal' (webhook) delivery with its status. This is the record to read when a piped-in value looks wrong or a customer system did not receive a signal. Empty for linear (non-graph) studies. Signals from a simulated interview are marked ``dry_run`` unless that run opted into real delivery.

Full transcripts for a study's interviews, newest interview first, paginated
by interview. Each transcript also carries ``variables`` — the answers that
interview captured into Interview Flow variables, empty for a study that
captures nothing. Filter with ``completed`` and ``include_simulated``. For a
single interview use ``GET /interviews/{interview_id}/transcript``.

Pass ``external_participant_id`` to fetch the transcripts of one person by
your own id for them — the id the entry link's ``?participant_id=`` or the
embed metadata bag carried. Each transcript carries that id back, so an export
can be joined to your own records without a second call.

get.description:
Search participant answers in a study.

* ``mode=string`` — full-text (websearch syntax: quoted phrases, ``-term``)
  fused with trigram fuzzy matching. No external services required.
* ``mode=semantic`` — embedding similarity over stored response vectors
  (query embedded with Voyage AI). Finds conceptual matches that share no
  words with the query. Only messages that have embeddings are searchable.
* ``mode=hybrid`` (default) — reciprocal-rank fusion of all three rankings;
  falls back to string-only behavior if semantic search is unavailable and
  ``strict`` is false.

Optionally scope to one question with ``question_id`` (questions-table ID, or
graph node ID for graph-mode studies).

parameters.name: question_id

schema.description: Restrict to one question. A questions-table id for a linear study, or a graph step id for a flow study — the step id you authored, exactly as ``get_graph`` reports it

get.summary: List questions eligible for an analysis view
get.description:
Questions of the study that fit the requested analysis ``category``:

* ``text`` — free-text questions (clusterable; includes distinct respondent counts)
* ``scale`` — scale questions with their scale config
* ``options`` — single-select and multi-select questions with canonical answer counts

For graph-mode studies, ``id`` carries the graph node ID.
Response count per scale value. Follow-up turns are excluded; out-of-range and non-numeric replies are skipped.
get.x-pp-example: deutero-pp-cli studies analysis get-scale-responses f1a767b5-3e58-4f5f-9575-611bf6886735 --question-id a8c57d33-afa8-4b68-99fb-dd8336442d3f

get.description:
Response count per option. Single-select answers match one option label
(translated answers are mapped back to the original option); multi-select
answers are JSON arrays whose every selected label is counted. Declined
answers are reported as a "Prefer not to answer" entry when present.

post.summary: Run k-means clustering on a question's responses
post.description:
Group participants' free-text answers to one question into themes.

Each participant's answers are condensed into a single vector, k-means sorts
those vectors into ``n_clusters`` groups, and every group is given a short
thematic label and summary. Labeling uses the platform's analysis model and is
best-effort: if it fails the groups are still returned, just with generic
labels.

No setup is needed — the vectors are computed automatically as interviews come
in. You only need enough answered responses to fill the requested number of
clusters; if there are too few, the call returns ``400`` (lower ``n_clusters``
or wait for more responses).

The result is saved: it appears on the study's Analyze page in the dashboard
and can be re-fetched later with ``GET .../clustering/latest``.

Suggests how many clusters to use for a question. Applies the elbow method to participants' response vectors and returns the suggested count as ``optimal_k``, plus the underlying inertia-vs-k curve (``k_values`` and ``inertias``) so you can plot the elbow yourself. Use the result as the ``n_clusters`` value for ``POST .../cluster``.

get.description: Returns the study's most recent saved clustering run, ready to chart: per-cluster point coordinates and centroids. ``exists`` is false when the study has not been clustered yet.

Every event an endpoint can subscribe to, what makes it fire, and the fields its payload carries — read this before creating an endpoint, so the subscription names events that exist and the receiver knows what it will get. ``interview.completed`` and ``interview.started`` carry ``external_participant_id``, your own id for the participant, which is what lets a receiver act on a finished interview without calling back.
Every webhook endpoint in your organization, newest first. Signing secrets are not included — they are shown only when an endpoint is created or its secret is rotated.

post.description:
Subscribe a URL of yours to organization events. The response carries the
**signing secret, the only time it is ever shown** — store it before doing
anything else, and verify every delivery against it.

The endpoint receives events for every study the organization owns. Name the
events you want in ``events``; an empty list means all of them.

patch.description: Partial update: only the fields you send change. Set ``enabled`` false to pause deliveries without losing the endpoint or its secret. Changing ``events`` replaces the subscription list rather than adding to it.

delete.description: Permanently removes the endpoint and its delivery log. To stop deliveries temporarily, set ``enabled`` false with update_webhook instead — deleting throws the signing secret away with the endpoint.

post.summary: Rotate a webhook endpoint's signing secret
post.description: Mint a new signing secret for this endpoint and return it — the only other time a secret is shown. **The previous secret stops verifying immediately**, so deploy the new one to your receiver before the next event fires, or expect signature failures in between. Use this when the secret from ``create_webhook`` was lost or leaked.

get.description: The delivery log for one endpoint, newest first: what was sent, who it was about, the status your server returned, and the error if it failed. This is the record to read when an expected event never arrived — a 4xx or a connection error here says the delivery was attempted and your receiver refused it, while no row at all says nothing fired (check that the endpoint is enabled and subscribed to that event type). Interview deliveries carry external_participant_id, your own id for the participant, so this log reconciles against your own records: success=false lists the people you were told about but may never have acted on, and external_participant_id=<id> shows every attempt for one person. Deliveries logged before that field existed report null.

estimated_credits.title: Estimated Credits
estimated_credits.description: Credits reserved for this run; the reservation is released if the run does not complete

persona_id.title: Persona Id
persona_id.description: Persona to play the participant. Omit to run against a generic participant, or pass ``persona`` to use ad-hoc text instead.

persona.title: Persona
persona.description: Ad-hoc persona description, used when no ``persona_id`` is given. Overrides the stored text if both are supplied.

model_tier.title: Model Tier
model_tier.description: Which model conducts and answers the interview: 'open_weights' (cheapest), 'standard' (Solo plan and up), or 'premium' (Team plan). Higher tiers cost more credits per run. The former name 'frontier' is still accepted and means 'premium'.

deliver_signals.title: Deliver Signals
deliver_signals.description: Let this run's 'Send a signal' steps reach their real endpoints. Off by default: a simulation records what each signal would have sent without sending it. When on, receivers get exactly what a live interview sends, plus an X-Deutero-Simulated header.

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Project to create the study in. The caller must belong to the organization that owns this project.

description.title: Description
description.example: How did you first hear about us?

survey_type.title: Survey Type
survey_type.description: Study methodology. One of: sociology, user_experience, customer_development, polling

model_tier.title: Model Tier
model_tier.description: Interview model tier: open_weights, standard, or premium ('frontier' is accepted as a deprecated alias for 'premium'). Only standard and premium can read image-upload answers.

redirect_url.title: Redirect Url
redirect_url.description: URL participants are sent to after completing. May contain {{external_participant_id}}, replaced with the id this interview arrived with (from the link's ?participant_id= or the embed metadata bag) — how a panel or CRM gets its own id handed back

voice_enabled.title: Voice Enabled
voice_enabled.description: Offer a voice-call interview link alongside text chat

video_enabled.title: Video Enabled
video_enabled.description: Offer a video-call interview link alongside text chat

redirect_url_warning.title: Redirect Url Warning
redirect_url_warning.description: Set only on a create/update that changed or questioned the redirect URL you sent — a single-braced placeholder corrected, or a placeholder we do not substitute. Null on reads

dashboard_url.title: Dashboard Url
dashboard_url.description: Researcher dashboard page for this study

participation_url.title: Participation Url
participation_url.description: Direct text-chat participant link (/chat?survey_id=...) — share this one for text interviews. Append &source=<campaign tag> and/or &participant_id=<your own id for this person> to record where the participant came from

short_participation_url.title: Short Participation Url
short_participation_url.description: Short text-chat participant link, if a short URL slug is set

voice_participation_url.title: Voice Participation Url
voice_participation_url.description: Direct voice-interview participant link, if voice_enabled

short_voice_participation_url.title: Short Voice Participation Url
short_voice_participation_url.description: Short voice-interview participant link, if voice_enabled and a short URL slug is set

video_participation_url.title: Video Participation Url
video_participation_url.description: Direct video-interview participant link, if video_enabled

short_video_participation_url.title: Short Video Participation Url
short_video_participation_url.description: Short video-interview participant link, if video_enabled and a short URL slug is set

description.title: Description
description.example: How did you first hear about us?

redirect_url.title: Redirect Url
redirect_url.description: URL participants are sent to after completing. May contain {{external_participant_id}}, replaced with the id this interview arrived with — the only placeholder understood

StudyUpdate.title: StudyUpdate
StudyUpdate.description: Partial update: only supplied fields are changed.

SuccessResponse.title: SuccessResponse
SuccessResponse.description: Generic acknowledgement for mutations that return no resource body.

external_participant_id.title: External Participant Id
external_participant_id.description: Your own id for this participant, from the entry link's ?participant_id= or the embed metadata bag's participant_id key — the id to join this record back to your own records by. Null when the interview arrived without one

web_source.title: Web Source
web_source.description: Campaign tag the entry link carried (?source=…); null when the link named none

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Answers this interview captured into flow variables — the structured values branching, piped text and downstream steps ran on. Empty for a study that captures nothing, including every linear study

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.description: Every Branch this interview passed through, in order, with the label chosen and the step it routed to. Empty for a linear study or a flow with no branching

questions.title: Questions
questions.description: One entry per validated question, in interview order

label.title: Label
label.description: How you will recognize this endpoint in the list

url.title: Url
url.description: Publicly reachable http(s) URL that receives the POSTs

events.title: Events
events.description: Event types to subscribe to. **An empty list subscribes to every event** — pass the ones you want to narrow it. Unknown names are dropped; call list_webhook_event_types for the catalogue.

signing_secret.title: Signing Secret
signing_secret.description: Standard Webhooks signing secret (whsec_…). **Shown once and never retrievable** — store it now, or call rotate_webhook_secret later for a new one. Verify every delivery against it before acting on the body

WebhookCreatedOut.title: WebhookCreatedOut
WebhookCreatedOut.description: A newly created endpoint, plus the one and only sight of its secret.

msg_id.title: Msg Id
msg_id.description: Value of the webhook-id header the receiver dedupes on

external_participant_id.title: External Participant Id
external_participant_id.description: Your own id for the participant this delivery was about, as it was sent in the event payload. Present on interview.started and interview.completed deliveries whose entry link carried one; null for every event that names no participant. Use it to reconcile what you were told against what you acted on — filter this endpoint by external_participant_id to find the deliveries for one person, or list the failures and read this field to see who was never successfully notified.

envelope.title: Envelope
envelope.description: Shape of every delivery body, whatever the event type

signature_headers.title: Signature Headers
signature_headers.description: Headers carrying the Standard Webhooks signature

data_fields.title: Data Fields
data_fields.description: Keys present in the envelope's ``data`` object

WebhookEventTypeOut.title: WebhookEventTypeOut
WebhookEventTypeOut.description: One subscribable event, with what it carries.

event_types.title: Event Types
event_types.description: Every subscribable event type, for convenience

events.title: Events
events.description: Subscribed event types; empty means every event

signing_secret.title: Signing Secret
signing_secret.description: The new signing secret. The previous one stops verifying immediately, so deploy this before the next delivery

events.title: Events
events.description: Event types to subscribe to. **An empty list subscribes to every event** — pass the ones you want to narrow it. Unknown names are dropped; call list_webhook_event_types for the catalogue.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: false pauses deliveries without deleting the endpoint

configured.title: Configured
configured.description: Whether a welcome message is set

message.title: Message
message.description: Welcome/consent message shown before the interview

consent.title: Consent
consent.description: Whether the participant must explicitly consent to proceed

target_language.title: Target Language
target_language.description: Target language name or ISO code (e.g. 'Spanish' or 'es')

source_language.title: Source Language
source_language.description: Source language name or ISO code

bearer_auth.bearerFormat: API key or Stytch M2M access token

tags.name: Welcome & Consent
tags.description: Pre-interview welcome message, consent gate, and translations.

tags.name: Characteristics
tags.description: Participant attribute questions collected before the interview.

tags.name: Credits
tags.description: Organization credit balances, usage, and reservations.

tags.name: Interview Questions
tags.description: The linear main question list (text, scale, choices, multi-select, ranking, card-sort, slots, image-upload).

tags.name: Interview Flow
tags.description: Branching graph-mode interview scripts: steps, conditional paths, captured answers, data fetches, and webhooks. The alternative to the linear question list.

tags.name: Recruitment
tags.description: Participation links, short URLs, quotas, and redirects.

tags.name: Response Monitoring
tags.description: Participation stats, interview lists, and transcripts.

tags.name: Personas & Simulation
tags.description: AI personas and the simulated interview runs that rehearse a study against them before real recruitment.

tags.name: Transcript Search
tags.description: Bulk transcript export and string/semantic/hybrid search over participant answers.

tags.name: Analysis & Clustering
tags.description: Scale/options response tallies and embedding-based k-means clustering with LLM-generated theme labels.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Organization-level event subscriptions: signed HTTP callbacks for interview, analysis, simulation, study and credit events. Distinct from the per-step signals an Interview Flow sends mid-interview.
